items.title: Kerala High Court upholds State's decision to abolish Kerala Police Officers Association
items.summary: A Division Bench of the Kerala High Court on Thursday set aside a single judge ruling that had quashed the State's decision to dissolve the Kerala Police Officers Association (KPOA), as part of its move to restructure associations formed by police officers in Kerala. [Addl R3 Sugunan AP v The Kerala Police Officer's Asssociation & ors] The dispute arose from a State Home Department order reorganising three associations representing different ranks of police personnel. The order resulted in the dissolution of one of the three police associations (KPOA), while the remaining two were to be retained in a reorganised form. The KPOA challenged the State's order and secured a favourable ruling from a single judge . This was challenged before a Division Bench of the Court in appeal. A Division Bench comprising Justice AK Jayasankaran Nambiar and Justice Preeta AK , allowed four appeals filed by the state and two police personnel, today, effectively restoring the abolition of the KPOA. The Bench held that the associations concerned had been formed by the government and that membership followed automatically from a police officer's rank. items.title: The ‘right to nominate’ under DPDP: A statutory right with no statutory procedure
items.summary: As more of a person’s life moves online, a need has emerged to address what happens when an individual dies or is unable to access their digital data due to incapacity. India’s new data protection law attempts to address this through the nomination right but leaves gaps that a data fiduciary must fill to comply with the legislation's objectives. Section 14(1) of the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 (“ DP Act ”) allows an individual, the data principal, to nominate any other person who may, on the data principal’s death or incapacity, exercise that individual’s statutory rights under the DP Act and the Digital Personal Data Protection Rules, 2025 (“ DP Rules ”). The Act grants the nominee broad authority to exercise powers as if stepping into the shoes of the data principal. Does the right to nominate fill the gap it was designed to fill? The gap the provision attempts to fill is genuine, but the machinery to operate it is thin. Further, because the law on whether digital personal data can be considered “property” capable of succession is still undeveloped, it can lead to conflict when an heir stakes a competing claim. items.title: Meat-eaters a security threat? Bengaluru’s Anekal meat shops shut ahead of Modi’s visit
items.summary: Meat shops in parts of Bengaluru’s Anekal taluk will remain shut for over a day ahead of Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s visit to the area on November 13, with the district administration invoking prohibitory powers under the BNSS citing security concerns. The order, issued on November 10 by Bengaluru Urban Deputy Commissioner and District Magistrate P S Kantharaju, prohibits the sale of meat within the limits of Jigani Town Municipal Council (TMC) and Kallubalu Gram Panchayat in Anekal taluk. The restriction came into effect at 6 am on Thursday, November 12, and will remain in force until 4 pm on Friday, November 13. The administration invoked Section 163(1) of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), 2023, following a request from the Bengaluru Rural District Superintendent of Police Chandrakanth MV. The police cited security arrangements for Modi and other Central and state dignitaries attending the Golden Jubilee celebrations of Prashanti Kutiram in Anekal. The event is being organised by the Swami Vivekananda Yoga Anusandhana Samsthana (S-VYASA). items.title: NALSAR University launches ODR Centre for Mediation to resolve consumer disputes
items.summary: National Academy of Legal Studies and Research (NALSAR) University of Law recently launched the NALSAR Online Dispute Resolution (ODR) Centre for Mediation. The ODR Centre has the active support of the Telangana State Legal Services Authority and the Telangana High Court, and is working with Webnyay for providing technology for online hearings, case and document management. The Centre was launched on November 7 in Hyderabad at a programme organised by the Telangana State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission. Justice Koshy said that mediation had to become an integral part of the consumer justice system rather than a step parties discovered only after years before a commission. items.title: Karnataka High Court refuses to quash SFIO case against Razorpay directors
items.summary: The Karnataka High Court recently refused to quash a Serious Fraud Investigation Office (SFIO) case against two directors of Razorpay, which involves allegations that the payment gateway facilitated the operation of a digital lending network that was controlled by Chinese entities [ Harshil Mathur & Anr v Union of India ]. The case involves allegations that Razorpay failed to carry out diligent Know Your Customer (KYC) procedures before onboarding Chinese-controlled digital loan apps as merchants on its platform. By a November 4 order, Justice M Nagaprasanna dismissed a plea by Razorpay's Director Harshil Mathur and its Managing Director Shashank Kumar (petitioners) to quash the case against them. The Court noted that case involved disputed questions of facts. It reiterated that the High Court cannot conduct a minitrial on such disputed allegations. The Court concluded that it is up to the petitioners to prove during a trial that they had not breached any of their fiduciary duties as directors of Razorpay.
